tagline: A capital scattered across islands — Helsinki's archipelago, the new eastern waterfront, and the busiest crossing in the Baltic.
summary: Finland's mobility heart is Helsinki, a city built on a peninsula and a scatter of islands — Suomenlinna, Vallisaari, Pihlajasaari, Lonna, Korkeasaari — all minutes offshore, with the new Kruunuvuorenranta waterfront district just across the bay. Municipal ferries already carry large volumes to Suomenlinna, and the Tallinn crossing is the Baltic's busiest passenger corridor. A clean foiling tier links the islands, the new eastern waterfront and the regional towns on a Nordic capital primed for electric transport.
why_marine_mobility: Helsinki is an archipelago city where the fast way between the centre, the islands and the new eastern districts is the water. Navier's Pioneer II flies the inner-archipelago mesh — Market Square to Suomenlinna, the cross-bay run to Kruunuvuorenranta, the coastal hop to Porvoo — silent and zero-emission, complementing the city's Kruunusillat bridge plans rather than competing with them, while the Quanta-LR opens the Tallinn and Stockholm trunks.

demand_signals.label: Suomenlinna ferry volume
demand_signals.note: The municipal ferry to the UNESCO sea-fortress is one of HSL's busiest water services, carrying very large year-round volumes on a ~1.5 nm hop — proven dense short-water demand.

demand_signals.label: Archipelago island cluster
demand_signals.note: Vallisaari, Pihlajasaari, Lonna and Korkeasaari (zoo island) are minutes offshore and draw heavy summer leisure traffic on slow seasonal boats.

demand_signals.label: Kruunuvuorenranta waterfront
demand_signals.note: A major new residential district across the bay from the centre — a fresh, high-density cross-water commuter corridor the city is building transit capacity for.

use_cases.body: A silent, on-demand foiling tier upgrading the Suomenlinna run and linking the new Kruunuvuorenranta district to the centre across the bay in minutes.
Fast archipelago shuttles to Vallisaari, Pihlajasaari and the zoo island that replace slow seasonal boats with frequent clean hops.
A premium Helsinki–Tallinn crossing and scenic coastal runs to Porvoo on stabilised, dry foiling craft.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The inner-archipelago mesh — Market Square↔Suomenlinna (~1.5 nm), Vallisaari (~2.5 nm), Pihlajasaari (~1.5 nm), Lonna (~1.2 nm), Korkeasaari (~2 nm), Kruunuvuorenranta (~2 nm) and the Porvoo coastal run (~26 nm) — sits inside the 70 nm all-electric range for high-frequency clean rotations off existing piers.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The Helsinki↔Tallinn crossing (~43 nm) is foilable directly, while the Helsinki↔Stockholm trunk (~210 nm across the Åland Sea) is a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor (H2 2026+) with no mid-sea charging dependency.

signature_routes.label: Helsinki Market Square ↔ Suomenlinna (all-electric sea-fortress hop)
Helsinki ↔ Tallinn — Gulf of Finland crossing (Quanta-LR)

transit_planning: For HSL (Helsinki Region Transport) or the City of Helsinki: a clean water tier integrated with the existing ferry remit and the Kruunusillat cross-bay strategy, off existing piers, serving the islands and the new eastern districts.
competitive_landscape: The water splits between the high-frequency but slow municipal Suomenlinna ferry, summer-only island boats, and heavy diesel car-ferries on the Tallinn and Stockholm trunks. None is foiling, on-demand or zero-emission across the urban mesh, and the city is actively rethinking cross-bay mobility.
regulatory_note: Urban water transport falls under HSL and the City of Helsinki ports, with Traficom as maritime regulator; the Tallinn corridor is an intra-Schengen EU crossing. Finland's clean grid and electrification policy make an all-electric fleet a natural fit, with HSL's water-transport remit a ready integration path.
seasonality: A pronounced summer peak (May–September) for island and leisure traffic with long Nordic daylight; Suomenlinna runs year-round. Winter sea ice in the inner gulf concentrates service on the open-water season, where foiling's smooth ride suits the short, choppy crossings.
